title: Phrasal verbs of the week
goal: Learn ten useful phrasal verbs and see how to use them in different sentences.
goal_it: Imparare dieci phrasal verbs utili e vedere come usarli in frasi diverse.

steps.title: Phrasal verbs: get up, come back
steps.title_it: Phrasal verbs: get up, come back
en: A phrasal verb is a verb with a small word (up, on, off, back...). The small word often changes the meaning, so learn the whole phrase together.
This week you will learn ten phrasal verbs. Come back to this page a few times during the week.
Important rule: some phrasal verbs can be separated by an object (turn the light on), but if the object is a pronoun (it, them, me, him), you must put it in the middle: turn it on, not turn on it.
it: Un phrasal verb è un verbo con una particella (up, on, off, back...). La particella spesso cambia il significato, quindi impara l'espressione intera.
Questa settimana impari dieci phrasal verbs. Torna su questa pagina più volte durante la settimana.

Regola importante: alcuni phrasal verbs si possono separare con il complemento (turn the light on), ma se il complemento è un pronome (it, them, me, him) va messo in mezzo: turn it on, non turn on it.

head: Phrasal verb
Meaning
Italiano
rows: to leave your bed after sleeping

examples.en: I get up at seven on weekdays.
examples.it: Mi alzo alle sette nei giorni feriali.

examples.en: What time did you get up this morning?
examples.it: A che ora ti sei alzato stamattina?

examples.en: He never gets up early at the weekend.
examples.it: Nel weekend non si alza mai presto.

examples.en: I'll come back at six.
examples.it: Torno alle sei.

examples.en: When did she come back from Spain?
examples.it: Quando è tornata dalla Spagna?

examples.en: Come back soon!
examples.it: Torna presto!

steps.title: Machines: turn on, turn off
en: Separable: turn on the light / turn the light on. With a pronoun: turn it on.
Separable: turn off the TV / turn the TV off. With a pronoun: turn it off.
it: Separabile: turn on the light / turn the light on. Con un pronome: turn it on.
Separabile: turn off the TV / turn the TV off. Con un pronome: turn it off.

head: Phrasal verb
Meaning
Italiano
rows: to start a light, a machine or a device
to stop a light, a machine or a device

examples.en: Can you turn on the light, please?
examples.it: Puoi accendere la luce, per favore?

examples.en: I turned the radio on.
examples.it: Ho acceso la radio.

examples.en: It's dark in here. Turn it on.
examples.it: Qui è buio. Accendila.

examples.en: Please turn off your phone in the cinema.
examples.it: Per favore spegni il telefono al cinema.

examples.en: She turned the oven off.
examples.it: Ha spento il forno.

examples.en: Don't forget to turn it off before you leave.
examples.it: Non dimenticare di spegnerlo prima di uscire.

steps.title: Clothes: put on, take off
en: Separable: put on a coat / put a coat on / put it on.
Separable when it means remove clothes: take off your shoes / take them off. Not separable for planes.
it: Separabile: put on a coat / put a coat on / put it on.
Separabile quando vuol dire togliere i vestiti: take off your shoes / take them off. Non separabile per gli aerei.

head: Phrasal verb
Meaning
Italiano
rows: to wear something, or to start playing music or a film
to remove clothes; also, when a plane leaves the ground

examples.en: Put on your coat. It's cold outside.
examples.it: Mettiti il cappotto. Fuori fa freddo.

examples.en: She put her glasses on to read the menu.
examples.it: Si è messa gli occhiali per leggere il menù.

examples.en: Let's put some music on.
examples.it: Mettiamo un po' di musica.

examples.en: Take off your shoes at the door, please.
examples.it: Togliti le scarpe all'ingresso, per favore.

examples.en: He took his jacket off because it was hot.
examples.it: Si è tolto la giacca perché faceva caldo.

examples.en: The plane took off ten minutes late.
examples.it: L'aereo è decollato con dieci minuti di ritardo.

steps.title: Information and effort: find out, give up
steps.title_it: Informazioni e impegno: find out, give up
en: Usually not separated. Often followed by that, when, what, if.
Separable: give up smoking / give it up.
it: Di solito non si separa. Spesso seguito da that, when, what, if.
Separabile: give up smoking / give it up.

head: Phrasal verb
Meaning
Italiano
rows: to discover a fact or get information
to stop trying, or to stop a habit

examples.en: I found out the truth yesterday.
examples.it: Ieri ho scoperto la verità.

examples.en: Can you find out when the shop opens?
examples.it: Puoi scoprire a che ora apre il negozio?

examples.en: She found out that the train was cancelled.
examples.it: Ha scoperto che il treno era stato cancellato.

examples.en: I gave up smoking two years ago.
examples.it: Ho smesso di fumare due anni fa.

examples.en: Don't give up! You're nearly at the top.
examples.it: Non mollare! Sei quasi in cima.

examples.en: They gave up the search when it got dark.
examples.it: Hanno interrotto la ricerca quando è calato il buio.

steps.title: Problems and plans: break down, look forward to
steps.title_it: Problemi e progetti: break down, look forward to
en: Not separable. It has no object: the car broke down.
A phrasal verb with a preposition. After to we use a noun or the -ing form.
it: Non separabile. Non ha complemento: the car broke down.
Phrasal verb con preposizione. Dopo to si usa un nome o la forma in -ing.

head: Phrasal verb
Meaning
Italiano
rows: when a machine or a vehicle stops working
to feel happy about something that will happen

examples.en: Our car broke down on the motorway.
examples.it: La nostra macchina si è guastata in autostrada.

examples.en: The washing machine broke down again.
examples.it: La lavatrice si è rotta di nuovo.

examples.en: We were late because the train broke down.
examples.it: Siamo arrivati in ritardo perché il treno si è guastato.

examples.en: I'm looking forward to the weekend.
examples.it: Non vedo l'ora che arrivi il weekend.

examples.en: We're looking forward to seeing you.
examples.it: Non vediamo l'ora di vederti.

examples.en: Are you looking forward to your holiday?
examples.it: Non vedi l'ora di andare in vacanza?

steps.q: Which phrasal verb means 'to discover a fact'?
steps.q_it: Quale phrasal verb significa 'scoprire un fatto'?
steps.why: Find out means to discover information.
steps.why_it: Find out significa scoprire un'informazione.

steps.q: The plane ___ at ten o'clock.
steps.q_it: L'aereo ___ alle dieci.
steps.why: A plane leaves the ground = takes off. In the past: took off.
steps.why_it: Un aereo che parte da terra = takes off. Al passato: took off.

steps.q: It is cold outside. ___ your jacket.
steps.q_it: Fuori fa freddo. ___ la giacca.
steps.why: Put on means to wear something. Take off is the opposite.
steps.why_it: Put on significa indossare. Take off è il contrario.

steps.q: What does 'give up' mean in 'She gave up smoking'?
steps.q_it: Che cosa significa 'give up' in 'She gave up smoking'?
steps.why: Give up + -ing means to stop a habit.
steps.why_it: Give up + -ing significa smettere un'abitudine.

steps.q: Our washing machine ___ yesterday, so we called an engineer.
steps.q_it: La nostra lavatrice ___ ieri, così abbiamo chiamato un tecnico.
steps.why: When a machine stops working, we say it breaks down.
steps.why_it: Quando una macchina smette di funzionare si dice break down.

steps.q: Which sentence is correct?
steps.q_it: Quale frase è corretta?
steps.why: With a pronoun (it, them, me), the pronoun goes in the middle: turn it on.
steps.why_it: Con un pronome (it, them, me) il pronome va in mezzo: turn it on.

steps.q: Which sentence is correct?
steps.q_it: Quale frase è corretta?
options: I'm looking forward to see you.
I'm looking forward to seeing you.
I look forward to saw you.
steps.why: In look forward to, the word to is a preposition, so we use the -ing form: seeing.
steps.why_it: In look forward to, to è una preposizione, quindi si usa la forma in -ing: seeing.

steps.q: Which pair of phrasal verbs has opposite meanings?
steps.q_it: Quale coppia di phrasal verbs ha significati opposti?
steps.why: Turn on starts a machine and turn off stops it.
steps.why_it: Turn on accende e turn off spegne.

steps.q: I usually ___ at seven o'clock on weekdays. (get up)
steps.q_it: Di solito ___ alle sette nei giorni feriali. (get up)
steps.why: In the present simple, I get up. With he or she: gets up.
steps.why_it: Al present simple: I get up. Con he o she: gets up.

steps.q: Can you ___ the light, please? It is dark. (turn on)
steps.q_it: Puoi ___ la luce, per favore? È buio. (turn on)
steps.why: After can we use the base form: turn on.
steps.why_it: Dopo can si usa la forma base: turn on.

steps.q: She ___ her shoes at the door and put on her slippers. (take off)
steps.q_it: ___ le scarpe all'ingresso e si è messa le pantofole. (take off)
steps.why: The sentence is in the past, so the verb is took off.
steps.why_it: La frase è al passato, quindi il verbo è took off.

steps.q: Don't ___! You are nearly at the top. (give up)
steps.q_it: Non ___! Sei quasi in cima. (give up)
steps.why: After don't we use the base form: give up.
steps.why_it: Dopo don't si usa la forma base: give up.

steps.q: I want to ___ what time the museum opens. (find out)
steps.q_it: Voglio ___ a che ora apre il museo. (find out)
steps.why: After want to we use the base form: find out.
steps.why_it: Dopo want to si usa la forma base: find out.

steps.q: We're looking forward ___ the holiday.
steps.q_it: Non vediamo l'ora di andare in vacanza.
steps.why: The phrasal verb is look forward to.
steps.why_it: Il phrasal verb è look forward to.

steps.q: He ___ from Rome last night. Now he is at home. (come back)
steps.q_it: ___ da Roma ieri sera. Ora è a casa. (come back)
steps.why: Last night is a finished time, so we use the past: came back.
steps.why_it: Last night è un tempo finito, quindi si usa il passato: came back.

steps.q: The film is over. Please turn the TV ___.
steps.q_it: Il film è finito. Per favore ___ la TV.
steps.why: Turn the TV off = stop the TV.
steps.why_it: Turn the TV off = spegni la TV.

steps.q: Build the sentence.
steps.q_it: Costruisci la frase.
answers: She put her coat on and left
steps.why: Put her coat on: the object (her coat) goes in the middle.
steps.why_it: Put her coat on: il complemento (her coat) va in mezzo.

steps.q: Build the sentence.
steps.q_it: Costruisci la frase.
answers: Turn it off before you go out
steps.why: With the pronoun it, we say turn it off, never turn off it.
steps.why_it: Con il pronome it si dice turn it off, mai turn off it.

steps.q: Build the sentence.
steps.q_it: Costruisci la frase.
answers: We found out the answer yesterday
steps.why: Found out is the past of find out. The time word goes at the end.
steps.why_it: Found out è il passato di find out. L'espressione di tempo va in fondo.

steps.q: Build the sentence.
steps.q_it: Costruisci la frase.
answers: Their car broke down on the motorway
steps.why: Broke down is the past of break down. It has no object.
steps.why_it: Broke down è il passato di break down. Non ha complemento.

cards.ex: I get up at seven on weekdays.
Can you turn on the light, please?
Please turn off your phone in the cinema.
Put on your coat. It's cold outside.
Take off your shoes at the door, please.
I found out the truth yesterday.
I gave up smoking two years ago.
Our car broke down on the motorway.
I'm looking forward to the weekend.
